findings.title: Discard racing direct-capture completion signs a soft-deleted record, writes DELETED-then-SIGNED custody, and answers bound:true

evidence.snippet: pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(`capture-session:${session.id}`)) — comment: a discard can never race a binding
tx.evidence.updateMany({ where: { id: evidence.id, status: { in: [CREATED, UPLOADING] } } }) — no deletedAt predicate

findings.observed: Completion serialises on the evidence lock and checks session ACTIVE/deletedAt only at entry; discard serialises on a different (capture-session) lock, sets deletedAt and appends EVIDENCE_DELETED while status is still UPLOADING. Completion's final claim does not test deletedAt, so it signs, timestamps and enqueues the deleted record; completeDirectCapture returns bound:true regardless of the session claim count.
findings.expected: Discard and completion must exclude each other (same lock) and the finalize claim must require deletedAt IS NULL; a failed session claim must not report bound:true.
findings.dataFlow: client /complete (long rehash) -> network drop -> user Discard -> deletedAt set + EVIDENCE_DELETED -> completion claim succeeds -> SIGNED record with deletedAt, custody DELETED then SIGNED, session DISCARDED not BOUND
findings.rootCause: Two different advisory-lock keys guard the same record; the finalize claim predicate omits deletedAt.
findings.blastRadius: Direct-capture records (mobile, extension, screen, continuous) whose completion request outlives the client.
findings.impact: A signed evidence record hidden from both the active list and the trash, with a self-contradicting custody chain and a false API answer. Bytes and hash are intact.
findings.reproduction: Start a large continuous completion, drop the client connection, press Discard while the server is hashing.
findings.runtimeProofIdea: Needs a deterministic interleave point inside completeEvidence after the entry checks (no injection hook exists).
findings.remediation: Take the capture-session lock in completeDirectCapture before completeEvidence (or the evidence lock in discard); add deletedAt: null to the finalize claim; derive bound from the session claim.
findings.acceptanceProof: Interleaved integration test: discard after entry check -> completion refuses, no SIGNED+deleted row.
findings.migrationBackfill: Query evidences with status SIGNED/REPORTED AND deleted_at NOT NULL AND lifecycle_state <> TRASHED.

findings.title: Acquisition statement says the capture session was 'started before the capture'; UC-1 and UC-2 open it after the capture and the server never checks

evidence.snippet: in a server-issued capture session started before the capture
const startedAtUtc = ...; capture = await captureFullPage(...); ... openWebSession(token, req.teamId) at :55

findings.observed: The extension captures the page, then opens the session; Android single screen capture opens it after frames exist. Manifest captureStartedAtUtc is never compared with CaptureSession.startedAtUtc.
findings.expected: Either open the session before capture and enforce manifest window ⊆ session window, or change the statement.
findings.rootCause: Statement written for the mobile path and reused for modes that do not satisfy it.
findings.impact: An untrue evidentiary statement about acquisition timing on customer-facing outputs.
findings.runtimeProofIdea: none — client source order is decisive
findings.remediation: Reorder clients and enforce the window server-side, or reword per mode.
findings.acceptanceProof: Server refuses a manifest whose captureStartedAtUtc precedes session start; statement test per mode.
findings.migrationBackfill: Existing UC-1/UC-2 outputs carry the statement; decide whether to annotate.

findings.title: 'Direct capture' provenance (e.g. 'PROOVRA's own adapter produced the bytes') is selected by the caller's mode string with no client proof
findings.observed: Any bearer (web JWT, script) can open a DIRECT_WEB_CAPTURE_EXTENSION or DIRECT_SCREEN_CAPTURE_IOS session, upload arbitrary files plus a self-written manifest, and seal; outputs then say PROOVRA captured them. No limitation code discloses that the capturing client was unverified.
findings.expected: Direct-capture statements only when the client is authenticated as that adapter (extension-scoped token for UC-1, device binding for native), or a limitation disclosing unverified client.
findings.dataFlow: open(mode) -> reserve -> declare -> complete -> acquisitionMode -> statement
findings.rootCause: Mode is a caller-supplied enum; no binding between token audience/device and mode.
findings.reproduction: curl open with mode DIRECT_SCREEN_CAPTURE_IOS using a web session token, upload PNGs + manifest, complete.
findings.runtimeProofIdea: Integration: open session with web JWT for every mode -> accepted.
findings.remediation: Bind mode to token scope/audience (extension token only for UC-1; native app attestation or at least app-scoped token for UC-2..UC-5); add a CLIENT_NOT_VERIFIED limitation otherwise.
findings.acceptanceProof: Web JWT opening a DIRECT_* session is refused or labelled.
findings.ownerDecision: How strong must the client binding be (scoped token vs attestation)?

findings.title: Extension OAuth accepts any chromiumapp.org extension id when EXTENSION_OAUTH_REDIRECT_ALLOW is unset, with no consent step
findings.observed: Fail-open allow-list; authorize issues a code using the ambient session and redirects immediately. A third-party extension can silently obtain a capture.direct token able to create evidence and presign parts on the user's unsealed evidence.
findings.expected: Fail closed without a configured extension id; show consent.
findings.blastRadius: Users with a hostile browser extension installed.
findings.impact: Silent token issuance to arbitrary extensions.
findings.reproduction: Call authorize with redirect https://<32 a-p>.chromiumapp.org/ while signed in.
findings.remediation: Fail closed when unset; add a consent screen.
findings.ownerDecision: Confirm whether EXTENSION_OAUTH_REDIRECT_ALLOW is set in production (not readable from this audit).

findings.title: No reaper for ACTIVE/INTERRUPTED direct-capture sessions; the extension never discards, so failed captures leave permanent empty Evidence rows and orphan objects

evidence.snippet: no discard call exists in apps/extension/src

findings.observed: Sessions expire lazily only when the owner calls again; reserved CREATED evidence and S3 parts remain forever after a failure.
findings.expected: A reaper expires sessions and releases reserved records.
findings.impact: Orphan records (counted against FREE cap per commercial findings) and storage.
findings.remediation: Extend the reaper to ACTIVE/INTERRUPTED sessions past TTL; release reserved records.
